newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 6.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Telephone: 11-3324842, 11-3761233; Fax: 91-11-3351006 Internet : biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com
TOP STORIES
Hindustan Times
CBI INTERROGATES FORMER PRIME MINISTER RAO

Former Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao was interrogated for a second time by the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in connection with an alleged corruption scandal. Senior CBI officials spent nearly two hours with Rao.
Times Of India
PRIME MINISTER SAYS NOT UNDULY BOTHERED BY SCAM CASES

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said he was not unduly bothered by the consequences of judicial cases concerning various scams under investigation. He said the government would not meddle with the process of law. Gowda said his government did not believe in political witchhunts or vindictiveness while pursuing the various cases. Deve Gowda said he saw no threat to his government from the Congress party or if the United Front fared badly in the Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.
Economic Times
STATE BANK CUTS PRIME LENDING RATE BY 0.5 PCT

The State Bank of India (SBI) has announced one half of a percentage point cut in the prime lending rate (PLR) of 15.5 percent. The bank did not cut deposit rates. SBI's new PLR is exclusive of interest tax. Other public sector banks, such as Bank of Baroda and Corporation Bank, said they would revise their rates soon.
NAPHTHA PHASE-OUT FOR POWER COMPANIES LIKELY

The power ministry has proposed a gradual phase-out of naphtha as feedstock for power companies. This is in response to the projected shortfall in domestic naphtha production. Several power companies, which have proposed to utilise naphtha as fuel, are likely to be discouraged in view of the shortfall.
METDIST TO SET UP INDIA'S BIGGEST COPPER SMELTER

The chairman of the London Metal Exchange, Raj Bagri, a non-resident Indian, and Japan's Mitsubishi group are setting up India's biggest copper smelter project. The project is estimated to cost 19 billion rupees. Bagri's investment initially would be through Metdist Industries Ltd, a company promoted by the Metdist Group, U.K.. The Mitsubishi group's investment in the 150,000 tonne copper unit in Gujarat will be through Mitsubishi Materials Corporation.
TATA STEEL TIE UP $50 MLN EXTERNAL LOANS

The Tata Iron and Steel Company has tied up external commercial borrowings worth $50 million for its fourth phase of modernisation at Jamshedpur. Discussions are reported to be under way with ANZ Grindlays to tie up a part of this amount. A total of DM 33 million has been tied up through Hermes, $17 million through Citi Bank and $6 million through State Bank of India.
GOVERNMENT PROPOSAL FOR INFLATION-INDEXED BONDS

The Indian government has cleared a proposal sent by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for introducing inflation indexed bonds. The coupon of the indexed bonds would be linked to the movements in the wholesale price index. Central Bank sources said the RBI had suggested a three-year tenure for the indexed bonds. In the case of real interest rate, RBI had suggested a band of 2.2-3 percent, sources added.
Financial Express
BANKS SEEK UNIT SPECIFIC ACCOUNTS

Banks have initiated a move to make it mandatory for corporates to submit detailed balance sheets incorporating activities of other existing units as well as balance sheets of individual units. The measure would discourage diversion of working capital funds from profit-making units to the other weaker units of a company. Banking sources said plans were also afoot to make such diversion of funds a criminal offence, instead of the present civil one.
MOVE TO EASE CREDIT BURDEN ON EXPORTERS

The Reserve Bank of India, the central bank, is considering instructing banks to charge commercial rates of interest on post-shipment rupee credit only for the period exceeding 90 days, during which foreign exchange earnings remained to be realised by exporters. The RBI move is expected to significantly lower the burden from the high cost of credit available to exporters under the post-shipment credit scheme. Sources said this would also help exporters to face global competition.
STEEL MAJORS PLAN TO SET UP SEPARATE FORUM

Unhappy with the role of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), steel majors have formed an independent body to take up issues relating to the industry with the government. The new body would include Steel Authority of India Ltd, Rashtriya Ispat Nigam Ltd, Tata Iron & Steel Company Ltd and other major steel producers. The idea of an independent body was mooted in October 1994 and the need was felt more after the CII submitted a memorandum to the finance minister asking for a cut in customs duty on steel while retaining the excise duty at the same level.
Observer
INDIAN OIL MAY TAKE OVER HINDUSTAN FERTILISER'S HALDIA UNIT

Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) is finalising plans to take over the Haldia unit of Hindustan Fertiliser Corporation (HFC), closed since October 20, 1996. Haldia Refineries of IOC has submitted a feasibility report on the HFC unit to IOC board. If IOC takes over the ailing unit, this would be the first time that a public sector unit, which has failed to go on stream, is taken over by another public sector unit.
Business Line
MONETARY EXPANSION HIGHER

The performance of the economy in the first four months of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) presents a contrasting picture with lower inflation rate but a higher money supply growth. A finance Ministry report said between March 31 and July 19 this year monetary expansion was substantially higher at 3.9 percent compared to 1.4 percent in the corresponding period of 1995/96. However, on the sources side, the growth in net bank credit to government at eight percent was lower during the period under review. But Reserve Bank of India's net credit to the Central government showed an increase of 11.9 percent.
